title: TRADITIONAL VALUES (COMMUNAL EDITION)
about: A Gold-Class husband brings home a government form that would fold his marriage into the state; his wife reads it, says no, and answers with a form of her own, because in this Republic consent still outvotes a committee.

beats.text: A model home in a gated community where everyone has been told to read Plato. A marble Socrates sits on the counter where the fruit bowl should be.
see: a marble bust on a kitchen counter

beats.text: Babe! Okay. So. Great news.
No.
Okay, so, you know how the Board of Regents is modernizing marriage?
Marriage does not need an update. Marriage is not an app.
Chad lays an official form on the counter. The Board wants marriage run as a state program, and Chad has volunteered his. His wife reads it without blinking.
see: a government form on a table
a woman reading a document in a kitchen

beats.text: He is about to "tradition" his way into a divorce.
Plato says the family unit makes people selfish, right? So, we're doing family values... statewide.
That is not family values. That is you trying to outsource commitment like it's lawn care.
Okay, look. The state is simply recognizing your function.
My what.
Your function. Like, the soul has parts. And each part does its job. It's justice.

beats.ask: a marriage is between two people

beats.text: Becky reaches into her bag and slides a form of her own across the counter. It is already stamped and filed: a petition for divorce.
see: a woman sliding a paper across a table
a rubber stamp on a document

beats.text: What is that.
That's my signature.
But... we're not allowed to have private families.
Exactly.
So... how can you...
I'm not having a private family. I'm having a private exit.

beats.ask: I think she did the right thing

beats.text: Huey. Tell her this is justice.
Justice is each part doing its proper function. Her proper function appears to be leaving you.
Becky picks up her car keys. Her sister lives across town, in the Bronze class.
see: a woman picking up car keys

beats.text: Wait, babe, if you leave, what am I supposed to tell the Board?
Tell them your "traditional values" got outvoted by consent.
The door closes. Chad stands alone in the kitchen, holding a form he suddenly hates.
see: a man standing alone in a living room

beats.text: I just... thought... I thought Plato would make me... the good guy.
This is not a republic. This is an HOA with a reading problem.
